practice1.prompt: Use Python's built-in math library: print the square root of 16, pi, the cosine of 0 and the factorial of 5.

cases.name: prints the four values the library gives back
cases.expect_stdout:
Square root of 16: 4.0
Pi: 3.141592653589793
Cosine of 0: 1.0
Factorial of 5: 120

cases.name: the math library is imported
cases.describe: an import of the math module

cases.name: the values come from the library, not from typing
cases.describe: sqrt, cos and factorial actually called

practice1.hint: math.sqrt returns a float, so the square root of 16 does not print the way the whole number 4 does. Let the library produce each value rather than typing what you expect it to say.

questions.prompt: Which of these comes with Python, with nothing to install?
questions.explain: math, random, datetime, json, csv and os are part of the standard library. The other three come from PyPI and have to be installed first.

questions.prompt: Where do you run `pip install requests`?
choices: At the top of your Python file
In your terminal, before you run the program
Inside a function that needs it
questions.explain: pip is a command-line program, not Python syntax. Put it in a Python file and you get a SyntaxError.

questions.prompt: Match each external library to what it is for.
questions.explain: Knowing which library covers which job is most of the work of finding one. The names rarely say it on their own.

questions.prompt: The conventional way to bring in the plotting library is `import matplotlib.pyplot ___ plt`.
questions.explain: An alias shortens a long dotted name. plt is a convention rather than a rule, but almost every example you will read uses it.

questions.prompt: Which are reasonable ways to judge whether a library is worth using?
choices: It has documentation with worked examples
It is downloaded and used widely
Its issues show it is still maintained
questions.explain: Documentation, usage and recent activity all say something about whether you will be able to get unstuck. The name says nothing.

reflection-exercise1.hint: Say what has to happen before you can import each kind, and name one library on each side.

reflection-exercise2.hint: There are three forms worth knowing. Say what each one puts into your namespace, and when that is what you want.
